name: Hydrocortisone
summary: The physiologic glucocorticoid, used at replacement doses for adrenal insufficiency and at higher doses for its anti-inflammatory actions.
mechanism: Agonist at the glucocorticoid receptor with added mineralocorticoid activity, reproducing endogenous cortisol's metabolic and stress responses.
pharmacodynamics: At replacement doses restores cortisol physiology; at pharmacologic doses provides anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects plus sodium retention.

dosing.adult: Replacement: 15–25 mg/day in divided doses (e.g., 10 mg morning, 5 mg evening); adrenal crisis: IV 100 mg bolus then 50–100 mg every 6–8 h with stress dosing

safety.pregnancy: Physiologic replacement is generally considered safe in pregnancy
warnings: Mineralocorticoid effects (fluid retention, hypertension) more prominent than with prednisolone at high doses
HPA-axis suppression with prolonged supraphysiologic dosing — taper
Hyperglycemia, infection risk, osteoporosis with long-term use
safety.overdose: Hypertension, hyperglycemia, psychiatric symptoms; supportive care, no antidote

clinicalPearls: In adrenal insufficiency, double or triple the dose (stress dosing) during febrile illness — patients need education on this.
It provides partial mineralocorticoid activity; primary adrenal insufficiency may still need added fludrocortisone.
good: Physiologic replacement that covers both glucocorticoid and some mineralocorticoid needs.
bad: Short half-life requires multiple daily doses; mineralocorticoid effects at high doses.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard endocrinology/pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
